message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles UTC offset | Berlin UTC offset | Time difference (Berlin – Los Angeles) |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Standard time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Daylight‑saving time** (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Transition windows** | | | **+8 hours** (Berlin is 8 h ahead) |

### Why the difference can be 8 hours

- **US DST** starts on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November.  
- **European DST** starts on the last Sunday in March and ends on the last Sunday in October.

During the brief overlap when one region is on DST and the other is still on standard time, the offset difference shrinks to 8 hours.  
For example:

- **March 10–30** (2024): Los Angeles is on DST (UTC‑7) while Berlin is still on standard time (UTC+1) → 8 h difference.  
- **October 27–November 3** (2024): Berlin has switched back to standard time (UTC+1) while Los Angeles remains on DST (UTC‑7) → 8 h difference.

Outside those windows, the difference is consistently **9 hours** with Berlin ahead of Los Angeles.
